In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''moduli stack of formal group laws''' is a [[stack (mathematics)|stack]] classifying [[formal group]] laws and isomorphisms between them. It is denoted by <math>\mathcal{M}_{\text{FG}}</math>. It is a "geometric object" that underlies the [[chromatic homotopy theory|chromatic]] approach to the [[stable homotopy theory]], a branch of [[algebraic topology]].

Currently, it is not known whether <math>\mathcal{M}_{\text{FG}}</math> is a [[derived stack]] or not. Hence, it is typical to work with stratifications. Let <math>\mathcal{M}^n_{\text{FG}}</math> be given so that <math>\mathcal{M}^n_{\text{FG}}(R)</math> consists of formal group laws over ''R'' of height exactly ''n''. They form a stratification of the moduli stack  <math>\mathcal{M}_{\text{FG}}</math>.  <math>\operatorname{Spec} \overline{\mathbb{F}_p} \to \mathcal{M}^n_{\text{FG}}</math> is [[faithfully flat morphism|faithfully flat]]. In fact, <math>\mathcal{M}^n_{\text{FG}}</math> is of the form <math>\operatorname{Spec} \overline{\mathbb{F}_p} / \operatorname{Aut}(\overline{\mathbb{F}_p}, f)</math> where <math>\operatorname{Aut}(\overline{\mathbb{F}_p}, f)</math> is a [[profinite group]] called the '''Morava stabilizer group'''. The [[Lubin–Tate theory]] describes how the strata <math>\mathcal{M}^n_{\text{FG}}</math> fit together.
<!--This moduli stack is closely related to the [[moduli stack of elliptic curves]].{{vague}}

In characteristic zero, this moduli stack is very easy to understand: the quotient stack <math>\mathcal{M}_{\text{FG}} \times_{\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}} \operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Q}</math> is isomorphic to <math>B \mathbb{G}_m</math>, the [[classifying stack]] of line bundles. This can be thought of as a manifestation of the "thesis" of [[differential graded Lie algebra]]s.
